question: Which of these is NOT one of the core pillars of safe motherhood?

options.A: Postnatal care
options.B: Family planning
options.C: Mandatory retirement
options.D: Antenatal care

explanation: Easy pick! The real pillars are family planning, antenatal care, safe delivery care, and postnatal care.

question: Why must instrument packs inside an autoclave chamber be loosely arranged rather than tightly packed?

options.A: Loose packs dry much faster after the cycle ends
options.B: Tightly packed metal will melt from the intense heat
options.C: Air pockets help the machine reach high pressure quicker
options.D: Steam must circulate freely around every item

explanation: If packs are squeezed together, steam cannot penetrate the center, leaving some instruments unsterilized. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T68#GNS214_U1_T68_h2)

question: What is the main long-term risk of not getting enough calcium while you are a teenager?

options.A: Chronic tiredness and sudden muscle weakness
options.B: Lower bone strength and higher risk of weak bones in old age
options.C: Delayed puberty and slow height growth
options.D: Severe vitamin deficiency like rickets

explanation: That's right! Your teenage years are your main window to build strong bones. Missing calcium now can lead to easily broken bones when you're older.

question: What turns raw clinical numbers into useful clinical information?

options.A: Information is always stored exclusively on paper charts
options.B: Information requires no documentation in the medical record
options.C: Information places raw facts into a meaningful context
options.D: Information is gathered only by physicians during rounds

explanation: Data becomes information when we organize and interpret it so it actually helps us understand the patient's condition!

question: What usually happens when a hospital operates under a strict blame culture?

options.A: Patient satisfaction scores increase significantly
options.B: Staff members hide errors and near misses out of fear
options.C: Doctors and nurses collaborate more effectively
options.D: Clinical staff report every minor mistake immediately

explanation: Spot on! If people know they will be punished harshly, they naturally keep quiet to save their jobs—which puts future patients at risk.

question: How do we view sleep in modern physiology?

options.A: An active, organized physiological state
options.B: A purely psychological phenomenon
options.C: A complete shutdown of brain activity
options.D: A passive absence of wakefulness

explanation: You might think the brain switches off at night, but sleep is actually a busy, organized state managed by specific brain networks. Great job keeping up with your physiology!

question: Why do human-made disasters often cause deep psychological trauma and feelings of betrayal?

options.A: They never cause physical injuries, leaving survivors confused about danger
options.B: The element of human negligence or malice creates strong feelings of betrayal
options.C: Psychological symptoms disappear faster because the disaster is man-made
options.D: Victims are always blamed publicly for causing the emergency situation

explanation: That makes total sense—knowing an accident could have been prevented by someone else's carelessness leaves survivors feeling angry and deeply betrayed.

question: Why is food safety especially critical for patients with weakened immune systems?

options.A: Their bodies struggle to fight off foodborne infections
options.B: Bad water changes their skin color
options.C: Dirty food automatically stops medicines from working
options.D: Uncooked meat increases muscle mass too fast

explanation: Spot on! An immune system that is down cannot easily fight off germs from bad food, leading to serious illness.

question: Why is trapping blood inside the penis (veno-occlusive mechanism) so important?

options.A: It closes off the urethral opening to prevent fluid loss during arousal
options.B: It pumps extra blood directly from the deep dorsal vein into the glans
options.C: It traps blood inside the corpora cavernosa to build high internal pressure
options.D: It releases large amounts of nitric oxide to keep the smooth muscle relaxed

explanation: Wonderful! By stopping blood from draining out while more keeps flowing in, pressure builds up to create a firm erection.

question: How does showing respect for a family's household customs help your patient care?

options.A: It allows the nurse to change household rules permanently
options.B: It reduces the financial cost of medical supplies
options.C: It builds trust and encourages the family to cooperate with the care plan
options.D: It guarantees the patient will never experience complications

explanation: Brilliant! When people feel respected in their own homes, they trust you more—and a trusting patient is much more likely to follow your health advice.

question: What weather condition in tropical regions like Nigeria contributes greatly to skin fungal infections?

options.A: Frequent consumption of contaminated municipal water supplies
options.B: High environmental humidity and warm weather conditions
options.C: Lack of personal hygiene products in local markets
options.D: Widespread resistance to standard antibacterial vaccines

explanation: You got it! Fungi love warmth and moisture. Our wonderful tropical climate means we see plenty of superficial skin fungal infections in clinical practice.

question: Why are large-bore intravenous lines inserted immediately for a patient with heavy APH?

options.A: To allow rapid fluid replacement and emergency blood transfusion
options.B: To prevent the patient from moving her arms during contractions
options.C: To allow continuous measurement of deep core body temperature
options.D: To make it easier to administer daily oral vitamin supplements

explanation: Large-bore cannulas are necessary to quickly replace lost blood volume and prevent the onset of hypovolemic shock. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T017#GNS226_U2_T017_h6)

question: Why do milk-borne disease outbreaks often hit many people in a neighborhood all at once?

options.A: Many consumers drank from the same contaminated batch of milk
options.B: The illness spreads directly through person-to-person coughing
options.C: Public water systems carry the bacteria through house pipes
options.D: Local weather changes activate dormant spores in the air

explanation: Exactly! When a single contaminated batch of dairy is sent out to many local homes, it naturally causes a sudden cluster of sick people in the community.

question: How does fee-for-service differ fundamentally from capitation?

options.A: Providers are paid based on each specific test or treatment performed
options.B: Patients pay the doctor directly with farm produce
options.C: The hospital receives the exact same amount every month forever
options.D: No money changes hands until the end of the calendar year

explanation: Under fee-for-service, payment is tied directly to the volume of services rendered rather than a fixed advance sum per patient. [learn more](GST322_U4_T8#GST322_U4_T8_h5)

question: Which of these is NOT something a nurse checks for safety during a first home visit?

options.A: Safety and cleanliness of the water supply
options.B: Presence of loose rugs or cluttered walkways
options.C: Condition of electrical wiring and cooking areas
options.D: Availability of high-tech robotic surgery equipment

explanation: Correct! We don't expect high-tech operating theatre equipment in a house. Our focus is purely on everyday home safety hazards.

question: Why is understanding the family life cycle important for a community health nurse?

options.A: It determines exact genetic disorders in newborns
options.B: It helps predict the specific stressors and health needs a family faces at each age
options.C: It proves if the family is registered with local government
options.D: It allows you to calculate household income

explanation: Every life stage has its own unique health risks, helping you know what guidance or preventive care to offer next.

question: Why should a nurse keep sentences short and clear when speaking to a disaster survivor?

options.A: Survivors usually have poor hearing after a disaster
options.B: Trauma and shock impair concentration and memory
options.C: Long sentences cost too much valuable time
options.D: Hospital regulations require brief communication

explanation: High stress levels make it difficult for survivors to process complex information or long explanations. [learn more](GNS315_U5_T6#GNS315_U5_T6_h7)

question: How can NSAIDs cause trouble for a patient's kidneys?

options.A: By forcing the kidneys to excrete too much potassium
options.B: By directly destroying kidney nephrons with toxic chemical crystals
options.C: By causing the bladder to spasm and block urine output
options.D: By reducing blood flow to the kidneys through prostaglandin inhibition

explanation: Prostaglandins act like traffic controllers keeping renal blood vessels nice and open. Block them, and the blood supply to the kidneys drops. Good to watch out for in dehydrated patients! [learn more](GNS223_U5_T4#GNS223_U5_T4_h4)

question: What is the main purpose of the Tolerable Upper Intake Level (UL)?

options.A: To measure the absolute least amount of protein a sick patient requires
options.B: To identify the highest daily nutrient intake unlikely to cause harm
options.C: To determine the standard portion size for hospital meal trays
options.D: To calculate the minimum amount of calories needed to survive a fast

explanation: The UL acts as a safety guard, showing the absolute highest amount of a nutrient you can take daily before risking toxicity.

question: What does follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH) do in the ovaries?

options.A: It helps immature eggs inside the ovaries grow.
options.B: It causes the muscular wall of the uterus to contract strongly.
options.C: It immediately stops all blood flow to the endometrium.
options.D: It thickens the outer layer of the vaginal walls.

explanation: True to its name, FSH 'stimulates' the little follicles in the ovary so the eggs inside can grow and get ready for action.

question: Why should a nurse teach a patient with diabetic foot neuropathy to test bathwater with their elbow instead of their feet?

options.A: Numbness in the feet prevents the patient from accurately sensing water temperature, risking scald burns
options.B: Elbow skin contains specialized sweat glands that neutralize toxic minerals found in tap water
options.C: Hot water causes immediate and permanent paralysis of the small motor nerves in the toes
options.D: The skin on the feet is biologically incapable of absorbing heat evenly compared to the upper body

explanation: Because neuropathy takes away normal feeling in the feet, patients might step into water that's way too hot without realizing it until they get burned. Using the elbow helps keep them safe!

question: What is the main reason for writing a nursing diagnosis in a patient care plan?

options.A: To determine the total cost of hospital treatment
options.B: To replace the medical diagnosis given by the physician
options.C: To legally clear the nurse from liability
options.D: To guide the selection of appropriate nursing interventions

explanation: Correct! A nursing diagnosis highlights how the patient is responding to a health issue, which helps you decide what nursing actions to take next.

question: How does the myelin coating affect the speed of an electrical signal traveling down a nerve fiber?

options.A: It increases impulse speed via saltatory conduction
options.B: It has no effect on nerve conduction velocity
options.C: It stops the impulse entirely until it reaches a synapse
options.D: It slows impulse speed by creating resistance

explanation: Myelin acts like insulation on an electrical wire. It lets the signal jump rapidly from one node to the next, speeding things up tremendously!

question: A community health nurse organizes a blood pressure screening exercise at the local market. What level of prevention is this?

options.A: Primary prevention
options.B: Primordial prevention
options.C: Tertiary prevention
options.D: Secondary prevention

explanation: Screenings are designed for early detection of health problems so that intervention can start before complications develop. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T3#GNS225_U2_T3_h4)

question: What is the main job of mineralocorticoids in the human body?

options.A: Regulating sodium and fluid balance
options.B: Suppressing white blood cell activity
options.C: Increasing protein synthesis in muscles
options.D: Lowering high blood sugar levels

explanation: Mineralocorticoids (like aldosterone) work on the kidneys to manage salt (sodium) and water in your body. It's all about keeping your fluid balance steady!

question: In what position should the nurse place the body before rigor mortis sets in?

options.A: Supine with limbs neatly aligned
options.B: In a semi-Fowler position at 45 degrees
options.C: Prone with the head turned sideways
options.D: Sitting upright supported by pillows

explanation: Placing the body flat in a supine position with straight limbs prevents stiffness in awkward postures. [learn more](GNS221_U4_T10#GNS221_U4_T10_h4)

question: How are wearable health trackers beginning to influence professional health records?

options.A: By replacing the need for licensed nurses in hospital wards
options.B: By serving as the primary billing invoice for insurance companies
options.C: By feeding real-time patient metrics directly into clinical systems
options.D: By automatically prescribing medications without a doctor's order

explanation: Wearables like smartwatches are starting to integrate live patient data such as heart rate and activity into medical records. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T4#GNS113_U2_T4_h8)

question: What is a major feature of non-governmental organizations (NGOs) in the health sector?

options.A: They are fully funded by compulsory federal taxes
options.B: They only provide care within major urban teaching hospitals
options.C: They operate independently from direct government control
options.D: They are legally required to employ only government civil servants

explanation: NGOs run as private, independent bodies separate from state or federal government management, even though they often partner with the government.

question: What does the acronym IEC stand for in nursing and public health?

options.A: Information, Education, and Communication
options.B: Infection, Evaluation, and Control
options.C: Investigation, Education, and Counselling
options.D: Immunization, Environment, and Care

explanation: IEC stands for Information, Education, and Communication, which are the core pillars of public health outreach. [learn more](GNS124_U5_T2#GNS124_U5_T2_h1)

question: Why must a researcher use a retrospective study rather than a live experiment when studying the health effects of a toxic chemical spill?

options.A: It is unethical to intentionally expose people to toxins
options.B: People exposed to toxins refuse to talk to researchers
options.C: Historical records are always one hundred percent accurate
options.D: Prospective studies cannot measure chemical levels accurately

explanation: You nailed it! We can never put people in harm's way on purpose. Looking backward at an accidental past exposure is the only safe, ethical way to study it.

question: Why must insulin be given as an injection instead of swallowing it as a pill?

options.A: Injections allow insulin to bypass the liver entirely
options.B: Digestive enzymes in the stomach destroy the insulin molecule
options.C: Stomach acid turns insulin into a toxic compound
options.D: Oral pills are absorbed too rapidly to be safe

explanation: Exactly! Insulin is a protein, so the acids and enzymes in your gut would break it down before it ever reached your bloodstream if you swallowed it.

question: A patient with very low platelets needs to shave. What should you hand them?

options.A: A straight metal blade
options.B: A pair of sharp scissors
options.C: A disposable razor
options.D: An electric shaver

explanation: Safety first! An electric shaver prevents accidental nicks and cuts, keeping a low-platelet patient safe from bleeding.

question: What is a major ethical worry when using tele-nursing communication?

options.A: Preventing patients from buying medications at local pharmacies
options.B: Ensuring that nurses get paid a higher salary than physicians
options.C: Maintaining patient privacy and data confidentiality over digital networks
options.D: Eliminating the need to write nursing notes in patient files

explanation: Well reasoned! Sending health info over phones or the internet can expose it to unauthorized people, making data privacy a huge ethical duty for nurses.

question: What does the 'T' stand for in the TNM cancer staging system?

options.A: Tumor size and extent
options.B: Tissue toxicity
options.C: Total body weight
options.D: Treatment schedule

explanation: In the TNM system, T evaluates the size and direct extent of the primary tumor, N assesses lymph node involvement, and M checks for distant metastasis. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T6#GNS321_U1_T6_h5)

question: Why should ear drops (otic drops) always be warmed to room temperature before putting them in?

options.A: Warming increases the antibiotic power
options.B: Cold drops can instantly burst the eardrum
options.C: Cold medication is too thick to pass through the ear canal
options.D: Cold drops can shock the inner ear and cause severe dizziness

explanation: Putting ice-cold drops straight into the ear canal tickles the balance center in the inner ear the wrong way, triggering sudden vertigo and nausea. Always warm them in your hands first!

question: In what way do nurses act as safety guards when using an EHR system?

options.A: By reviewing computerized alerts and verifying medication orders
options.B: By writing paper security codes on the walls of patient wards
options.C: By restricting doctors from ordering any laboratory tests
options.D: By physically repairing broken computer keyboards and monitors

explanation: Nurses use their clinical judgment alongside system prompts to catch potential errors before they reach the patient. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T2#GNS113_U2_T2_h8)

question: Your study proves a new handwashing technique cuts down ward infections. Where should you explain how ward nurses can use this daily?

options.A: In the discussion and nursing implications section
options.B: In the abstract summary at the very beginning
options.C: In the methodology and participant selection chapter
options.D: In the raw data tables of the results section

explanation: This is where research meets the bedside—translating your findings into practical steps for everyday nursing care.

question: Which type of life event is most likely to lead to complicated grief?

options.A: Sudden and violent death
options.B: Moving to a brand new neighborhood
options.C: Expected death of an elderly grandparent
options.D: Gradual retirement from work

explanation: Sudden or traumatic losses catch the mind completely off guard, making them much harder to process right away.

question: Why do safety experts encourage a blame-free reporting culture in hospitals?

options.A: It encourages staff to report errors so systems can be fixed
options.B: It allows managers to punish careless workers more easily
options.C: It prevents nurses from ever making mistakes again
options.D: It stops patients from filing lawsuits against the hospital

explanation: Spot on! When nurses aren't afraid of being punished, they speak up about close calls. That honesty helps the whole team fix dangerous workflows.

question: Why must an HMO verify that a hospital has qualified staff before adding it to their network?

options.A: To make sure the hospital building is painted blue
options.B: To meet NHIA accreditation standards and protect patient safety
options.C: To reduce the number of patients visiting the clinic
options.D: To avoid paying taxes to the federal government

explanation: Accreditation requires proof of clinical competence and good facilities so that enrollees receive safe, high-standard medical care. [learn more](GST322_U4_T8#GST322_U4_T8_h3)

question: A patient asks for a safe way to cook potatoes on a low-fat diet. What should you suggest?

options.A: Baked or boiled without butter or sour cream
options.B: Pan-fried in rich bacon drippings for flavor
options.C: Deep-fried in vegetable oil until golden brown
options.D: Smashed with heavy whipping cream and whole milk

explanation: Exactly! Potatoes are naturally fat-free, but you must skip the added butter, cream, or oils.

question: How does ethical leadership by a senior nurse affect junior staff members?

options.A: It forces them to focus solely on administrative paperwork over patient care
options.B: It teaches them how to bypass financial regulations without getting caught
options.C: It encourages them to ignore hospital policies when tasks become difficult
options.D: It inspires them to practice with integrity and high professional standards

explanation: Junior nurses learn so much by watching seniors. When leaders model strong ethics, it sets a wonderful, professional tone for the whole ward!

question: What is a great way to encourage nurses to speak up and report clinical errors or near-misses?

options.A: Reducing the salary of staff working in busy wards
options.B: Hiding all incident reports from hospital management
options.C: Fostering a supportive, non-punitive reporting culture
options.D: Firing any nurse who makes a minor documentation mistake

explanation: You got it! When nurses know they won't be unfairly witch-hunted for speaking up, they feel safe reporting mistakes so the whole hospital can learn and fix the system.

question: A junior nurse is told to do a dressing change a certain way simply because 'that is how we've always done it here.' What type of inquiry is this?

options.A: Traditional and authority-based inquiry
options.B: Randomized controlled testing
options.C: Empirical scientific inquiry
options.D: Systematic qualitative inquiry

explanation: Relying on past custom and instructions from senior staff without checking the literature is traditional and authority-based inquiry.

question: What does the term 'reduction' mean in the management of fractures?

options.A: Gradual shrinking of local soft tissue swelling using ice packs
options.B: Lowering the patient's blood pressure prior to orthopedic surgery
options.C: Surgical removal of dead bone tissue from an infected site
options.D: Realignment of the broken bone fragments into their normal position

explanation: Reduction is the process of putting displaced bone ends back into their correct anatomical alignment so they can heal properly. [learn more](GNS221_U3_T13#GNS221_U3_T13_h5)

question: When a patient eats a heavy protein meal, which hormone is released to trigger heavy acid and enzyme production?

options.A: Thyroxine
options.B: Insulin
options.C: Glucagon
options.D: Gastrin

explanation: Gastrin is the signal booster! When protein arrives and stretches the stomach, gastrin is released to tell the stomach to produce more acid for digestion.

question: Which serious condition involves tissue damage and inflammation in the bowels of a premature baby?

options.A: Retinopathy of prematurity
options.B: Transient tachypnea of the newborn
options.C: Necrotizing enterocolitis
options.D: Intraventricular hemorrhage

explanation: Necrotizing enterocolitis (NEC) is a tough bowel complication in preemies where parts of the intestine can suffer tissue death. You're mastering complex neonatal nursing topics!

question: A nurse manager checks if staff are following the correct aseptic technique during wound dressing changes. Which type of standard is being evaluated?

options.A: Structure standards
options.B: Outcome standards
options.C: Process standards
options.D: Legislative standards

explanation: Process standards look at the actual steps and actions nurses perform while carrying out patient care duties. [learn more](GST321_U1_T20#GST321_U1_T20_h2)

question: Why do hospitals require independent double-checks for high-risk medications?

options.A: To ensure that two nurses share the blame if a patient is harmed
options.B: To provide a redundant barrier that catches individual calculation errors
options.C: To waste nursing time and slow down medication administration
options.D: To prove to hospital management that staffing levels are adequate

explanation: Two pairs of eyes are better than one! Having a colleague double-check a calculation creates a safety net to catch accidental errors before they reach the patient.

question: A working mother needs daytime care for her two-year-old toddler. Which facility type is most appropriate?

options.A: An adult day care centre
options.B: A university lecture hall
options.C: A residential boarding home
options.D: An infant and toddler nursery

explanation: A two-year-old falls into the toddler category, making an infant and toddler nursery the correct setting for age-appropriate physical care and safety. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T7#GNS225_U4_T7_h3)

question: Which amino acid do renal tubule cells break down to produce ammonia and help buffer acid?

options.A: Glucose
options.B: Sodium
options.C: Albumin
options.D: Glutamine

explanation: When facing long-term acid buildup, kidney cells break down the amino acid glutamine to make ammonia, which acts as a shield to catch extra acid.

question: What is the main job of muscle spindles?

options.A: To measure the amount of tension placed on a tendon
options.B: To stop muscles from contracting when they get too tired
options.C: To provide energy for the muscle cells during hard work
options.D: To monitor changes in muscle length and stretch speed

explanation: Muscle spindles act like tiny built-in stretch detectors inside your muscles, keeping track of how fast and how far the muscle is stretching.

question: Where is the median cubital vein located, which is a favourite spot for starting an IV?

options.A: Near the inside of the ankle joint
options.B: Along the lateral side of the upper arm
options.C: On the back of the hand
options.D: In the antecubital fossa of the elbow

explanation: Exactly! The median cubital vein sits right across the bend of the elbow (the antecubital fossa), making it super accessible for quick IV lines and blood tests.

question: What is the main public health step used to stop leprosy from spreading in a town or village?

options.A: Finding cases early and starting treatment right away
options.B: Washing living areas with heavy chemicals
options.C: Locking all infected people away in isolated camps
options.D: Giving mandatory vaccines to every newborn baby

explanation: Catching cases early and starting medications quickly stops the spread because treatment makes patients non-infectious! Public health in action!

question: If a community shows both a high Maternal Mortality Ratio and a high Total Fertility Rate, what is the most likely link?

options.A: Contraceptive methods are causing direct medical toxicity
options.B: Frequent pregnancies without adequate spacing strain maternal health
options.C: Women are choosing surgical sterilization too early in life
options.D: Hospital records are systematically miscalculated by local staff

explanation: When pregnancies happen back-to-back without enough resting time, a mother's body gets worn out, which sadly drives up complication and mortality rates.

question: Which physical sign is a classic clue that a patient might have iron deficiency anemia?

options.A: Swollen bleeding gums
options.B: Enlarged thyroid gland
options.C: Pale conjunctiva
options.D: Dry brittle hair strands

explanation: When iron is low, hemoglobin drops, making the inner eyelids (conjunctiva) look unusually pale instead of a healthy pink.

question: What does Basal Metabolic Rate (BMR) actually measure?

options.A: The total calories burned during heavy physical exercise
options.B: The energy needed to maintain basic life functions at rest
options.C: The amount of heat produced during food digestion
options.D: The maximum oxygen consumption during endurance training

explanation: Think of BMR as your body's idle speed. It's the bare minimum energy required to keep your heart pumping, lungs breathing, and organs working while you do absolutely nothing.

question: What is the best eating strategy for an HIV patient dealing with severe nausea?

options.A: Avoiding all fluids for twelve hours
options.B: Eating three large oily meals daily
options.C: Consuming heavy, highly spiced foods
options.D: Eating small, frequent, bland meals

explanation: Correct! Small, gentle meals keep the stomach from feeling overloaded and help keep nausea at bay.

question: Which international agreement is specifically dedicated to stopping discrimination against women?

options.A: UNICEF
options.B: CEDAW
options.C: AFCTA
options.D: WHO

explanation: CEDAW stands for the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women—a key global pact for women's rights!

question: Why is the adhesive tape test preferred over a regular stool sample for diagnosing pinworms?

options.A: Stool samples destroy pinworm eggs due to high digestive enzyme levels
options.B: Stool microscopy cannot detect any form of nematode whatsoever
options.C: Pinworm larvae hatch instantly once they come into contact with water
options.D: Female pinworms lay eggs on the perianal skin rather than inside the feces

explanation: Since pinworms lay their eggs outside the bowels on the skin around the anus, regular stool tests usually miss them. That's why the tape test works best!

question: What is the main goal of performing a comprehensive nutritional assessment in a hospital setting?

options.A: Determining when the patient can be safely discharged home
options.B: Calculating the exact hospital bill for food services
options.C: Identifying existing or potential risks for malnutrition
options.D: Testing the patient's personal knowledge of grocery shopping

explanation: Assessment helps nurses catch nutritional deficits early so appropriate dietary interventions can be started promptly. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T015#GNS227_U2_T015_h8)

question: Which of these groups is considered a vulnerable population needing extra research protection?

options.A: Licensed physicians
options.B: Children
options.C: Hospital administrators
options.D: Healthy adult researchers

explanation: Correct! Children cannot give adult consent and have limited autonomy, so we must protect them extra carefully.

question: Why are first aid stations spread out across different areas of a huge venue?

options.A: To prevent attendees from finding the medical tents
options.B: To ensure injured patients can receive treatment quickly without traveling far through crowds
options.C: To ensure all medical supplies are kept in a single warm room
options.D: To reduce the number of nurses needed to staff the event

explanation: Spreading out medical posts means faster help for patients and fewer injured people trying to crawl through heavy crowds.

question: Which special property sets a ratio scale apart from an interval scale?

options.A: The presence of unequal intervals between numbers
options.B: The use of categories that cannot be ranked
options.C: The complete absence of any numerical values
options.D: The presence of an absolute true zero point

explanation: A true zero means zero actually means none of that item exists (like 0 mL of urine output). That's what makes it a ratio scale!

question: Which condition is a clear indication for using a warm poultice?

options.A: A widespread whole-body viral fever
options.B: A brand new ankle sprain with active bleeding
options.C: A localized boil or deep muscle ache
options.D: An area of skin with complete loss of sensation

explanation: Poultices work best on localized aches, stiffness, and closed infections like boils. [learn more](GNS221_U3_T10#GNS221_U3_T10_h4)

question: What is your absolute priority nursing action when a patient starts having a tonic-clonic seizure in bed?

options.A: Leave the bedside immediately to find the attending medical doctor
options.B: Lower the bed, clear nearby hazards, and turn the patient onto their side
options.C: Force a padded tongue depressor between the patient's teeth immediately
options.D: Restrain the patient's arms and legs tightly to prevent injury from flailing

explanation: Safety first! Keep the airway clear by rolling them onto their side and protect them from hitting nearby objects. Never stick anything in their mouth or hold them down.

question: Which hormone is mainly responsible for triggering the milk 'let-down' reflex when breastfeeding?

options.A: Oxytocin
options.B: Progesterone
options.C: Estrogen
options.D: Insulin

explanation: Wonderful! Oxytocin makes tiny muscles around the milk glands squeeze, pushing the milk forward for the baby. It's also the hormone of love and bonding!

question: Why do many developing countries often need external health support and international aid?

options.A: Private hospitals refuse to treat patients without foreign backing
options.B: International donors legally mandate that local taxes be abolished
options.C: Government health budgets often fall short of recommended funding targets
options.D: Citizens prefer foreign organizations over government clinics

explanation: When national funding isn't enough to cover public health needs, external donations step in to help keep clinics open and running.

question: At what level does management happen in a hospital?

options.A: Only at the executive board room level
options.B: Exclusively within the hospital pharmacy department
options.C: At every level from charge nurse to director
options.D: Strictly during annual government audits

explanation: Management isn't just for bosses in suits! From frontline charge nurses managing the ward to senior directors, everyone plays a leadership role.

question: A resident needs physical help to cut their food and bring it to their mouth. Which daily living activity does this fall under?

options.A: Bathing
options.B: Feeding
options.C: Transferring
options.D: Toileting

explanation: Well done! Eating and drinking assistance is classified under the feeding category of ADLs.

question: What happens to the mother's heart output right after the placenta is delivered?

options.A: It drops instantly to zero until diuresis begins
options.B: It experiences an initial rapid increase due to autotransfusion
options.C: It remains completely steady for exactly six weeks
options.D: It reverses direction and flows backward into the veins

explanation: You got it! Blood rushing back from the placenta temporarily boosts the heart's output right after delivery.

question: How do telehealth and remote monitoring help keep patients out of the hospital?

options.A: By eliminating all potential health risks associated with aging at home
options.B: By allowing nurses to catch early signs of clinical deterioration and intervene quickly
options.C: By stopping clients from taking prescribed medications incorrectly
options.D: By forcing clients to visit the outpatient clinic every single day

explanation: Catching small changes early means the care team can step in and fix things before a minor issue turns into an emergency. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T4#GNS113_U3_T4_h5)

question: What is the very first step a nurse should take after sustaining a needle stick injury while on duty?

options.A: Hide the incident from the supervisor to avoid paperwork
options.B: Report the incident immediately for evaluation and prophylaxis
options.C: Soak the injured finger in cold river water
options.D: Take a strong painkiller and finish the remaining shift

explanation: Always report immediately! Quick action allows the occupational health team to give you prompt counseling and protective meds.

question: Why do bad rural feeder roads hurt national food security?

options.A: They force the government to import all staple foods
options.B: They delay transport, causing high spoilage rates and high food prices in cities
options.C: They stop farmers from getting chemical fertilizers and seeds
options.D: They make it illegal for farmers to sell crops across state lines

explanation: When roads are poor, food gets stuck or damaged on the way, leading to waste and higher prices for people in the city.

question: Which organization sets the foundational legal and professional practice boundaries for nurses in Nigeria?

options.A: National Union of Local Government Employees
options.B: West African Health Education Board
options.C: Nursing and Midwifery Council of Nigeria (NMCN)
options.D: Nigerian Medical Association Financial Committee

explanation: The NMCN is the statutory body responsible for regulating nursing education and practice in Nigeria. [learn more](GST321_U1_T20#GST321_U1_T20_h5)

question: What is the main job of a mechanical ventilator in the ICU?

options.A: To replace the function of the human heart
options.B: To assist or take over the work of breathing
options.C: To increase blood pressure in shock patients
options.D: To cure underlying lung diseases permanently

explanation: Think of the ventilator as an extra pair of lungs! It helps or completely takes over breathing to keep oxygen flowing while the patient's body heals. You've got this!

question: A community has strong local leadership and plenty of food supplies even though droughts happen often. What do we call these strengths?

options.A: A structural mitigation measure
options.B: An indicator of high vulnerability
options.C: A primary environmental hazard
options.D: A community capacity resource

explanation: Well done! Capacities are simply the strengths and resources a community uses to stand strong against disasters.

question: On which side of the patient should a nurse stand when assisting them to walk with a gait belt?

options.A: At least two meters ahead of them
options.B: On the patient's weaker side
options.C: Directly behind the patient's back
options.D: On the patient's stronger side

explanation: Standing on the weaker side allows the nurse to provide the necessary physical support if the patient begins to lean or buckle. [learn more](GNS324_U6_T3#GNS324_U6_T3_h3)

question: Why might a patient with an enlarged heart (specifically an enlarged left atrium) find it hard to swallow?

options.A: The atrium presses directly against the anterior wall of the adjacent oesophagus.
options.B: Compression shuts down the vagus nerve endings supplying the stomach.
options.C: The heart enlargement blocks blood flow through the surrounding thoracic duct.
options.D: The diaphragm is pushed upward and prevents the lower sphincter from opening.

explanation: Makes total sense when you picture it: the left atrium sits right in front of the middle of the oesophagus, so if the heart swells, it pushes against the food pipe and narrows it!

question: Why are accurate health records so important in busy primary health care clinics?

options.A: They ensure continuity of care when different health workers see the same patient over time.
options.B: They are used to calculate monthly staff salaries.
options.C: They replace physical exams when the clinic is crowded.
options.D: They guarantee the clinic gets international donor funds.

explanation: Patients often see different nurses on different days. Good records ensure the next nurse knows exactly what treatment was given, keeping the patient safe and cared for smoothly!

question: A manager watches a nurse perform a sterile dressing change to ensure correct technique. What type of control is this?

options.A: Feedforward control
options.B: Concurrent control
options.C: Financial control
options.D: Feedback control

explanation: Observing care as it happens lets the manager catch and fix mistakes on the spot. That's concurrent control!

question: How does a dangerously fast heart rate hurt the heart's own blood supply?

options.A: It shortens the resting phase when the heart fills with blood.
options.B: It blocks the electrical signals from the SA node.
options.C: It increases the pressure inside the coronary sinus.
options.D: It causes the aortic valve to close too early.

explanation: Exactly! When the heart beats too fast, diastole gets too short, meaning the heart muscle misses out on its proper resting and feeding time.

question: What statistical measurement is primarily used in case-control studies?

options.A: Incidence rate
options.B: Odds ratio
options.C: Attributable risk
options.D: Relative risk

explanation: You got it! Because we start by looking at who is sick versus healthy, we calculate the 'odds ratio' to check for a link.

question: Why do patients often forget to mention herbs and local remedies during a drug history?

options.A: These substances dissolve completely in the body within minutes
options.B: Doctors automatically know every herb sold in local markets
options.C: They view them as food or lifestyle items, not real drugs
options.D: Federal law prohibits patients from discussing herbs in hospitals

explanation: Patients view everyday teas and herbal mixtures as harmless, so they don't think to mention them. Asking probing questions bridges this gap!

question: What is one major limitation of using robots in patient care units?

options.A: Robots require continuous physical lifting from bedside nurses
options.B: Robots lack clinical intuition and cannot interpret subtle human emotional cues
options.C: Robots completely eliminate the need for electronic health records
options.D: Robots are incapable of moving along hospital corridors

explanation: Spot on! Machines follow strict programming. They can never fully replace the warm, empathetic touch and observant eye of a real nurse.

question: What is the difference between a felt need and a real need in community health?

options.A: A felt need is what the community asks for, while a real need is what data shows they lack
options.B: A felt need can be solved with money, while a real need requires federal approval
options.C: A felt need is written in hospital books, while a real need is spoken secretly
options.D: A felt need affects children, while a real need only affects elderly men

explanation: Communities often request things like a big hospital building, when data shows their actual greatest need is clean drinking water to stop cholera. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T6#GNS124_U3_T6_h5)

question: According to the World Health Organization, what is the standard age range for adolescence?

options.A: Ages 10 to 19 years
options.B: Ages 5 to 12 years
options.C: Ages 15 to 25 years
options.D: Ages 12 to 21 years

explanation: The World Health Organization defines adolescence as the period between 10 and 19 years of age. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T4#GNS312_U3_T4_h1)

question: Which of the following is NOT a focus area during a health inspection survey in an SNF?

options.A: Infection control practices and hand hygiene compliance
options.B: Medication administration safety and storage
options.C: Stock market investments of the facility parent corporation
options.D: Resident rights and protection from abuse or neglect

explanation: Health inspectors look at patient safety, care quality, and resident rights—not corporate financial portfolios!

question: What is one exciting benefit expected from future voice-activated documentation tools?

options.A: Allowing nurses to speak clinical notes while performing procedures
options.B: Replacing the need for doctors to write prescriptions
options.C: Automatically bathing patients using robotic spray systems
options.D: Eliminating all hospital noise during the night shift

explanation: Brilliant! Voice tech aims to save us time by letting us dictate our notes hands-free while we work.

question: Which group of vitamins is more likely to build up in the body and cause toxicity if taken in excess for a long time?

options.A: Ascorbic acid compounds
options.B: Water-soluble vitamins
options.C: Fat-soluble vitamins
options.D: B-complex vitamins

explanation: Exactly! Fat-soluble vitamins get stored in the liver and fatty tissues instead of being peed out, so too much can cause a buildup.

question: Why do you need your nursing clinical judgment when reading a scatter diagram?

options.A: To calculate the exact square root of every data point
options.B: To draw the axes without using a ruler or computer
options.C: To eliminate the need for any further statistical tests
options.D: To decide if the visual relationship makes biological sense

explanation: Always ask yourself: does this relationship actually make sense in real healthcare practice, or is it just a random coincidence?

question: Which of these items goes into the sharps container?

options.A: Human tissues and body parts
options.B: Office paper and food packaging
options.C: Used hypodermic needles and scalpels
options.D: Expired tablets and liquid syrups

explanation: Sharps are anything that can cut or poke your skin, like needles, blades, and broken glass. Always drop them straight into a puncture-proof box!

question: What is a key duty of healthcare leaders when it comes to safety culture?

options.A: Delegating all safety duties to junior nursing students
options.B: Reducing the number of safety meetings in the hospital
options.C: Punishing staff publicly for every reported mistake
options.D: Allocating resources and listening to frontline concerns

explanation: Good leaders back up their words with action by giving nurses the tools, time, and a listening ear to keep patients safe.

question: When should a nurse hold off on starting AROM exercises?

options.A: Mild fatigue from staying in bed
options.B: A recent unstable bone fracture
options.C: A history of chronic mild backaches
options.D: Stable and well-controlled high blood pressure

explanation: Safety first! Moving a broken, unstable bone before it heals can displace it and cause serious harm.

question: What is the primary trigger for a cardiac action potential across cell membranes?

options.A: Movement of ions like sodium and potassium
options.B: Release of stored oxygen molecules in the tissue
options.C: Sudden changes in the temperature of the blood
options.D: Direct stimulation by circulating red blood cells

explanation: Cardiac cells generate electrical activity by rapidly shifting ions like sodium, potassium, and calcium across their membranes. [learn more](GNS223_U1_T3#GNS223_U1_T3_h1)

question: Why is continuous cardiac monitoring especially important for patients recovering from a heart attack?

options.A: It prevents them from moving around too much in bed
options.B: It automatically delivers shock therapy when needed
options.C: It helps catch dangerous rhythm changes early
options.D: It replaces the need for manual pulse checks completely

explanation: Damaged heart muscle after a heart attack can easily trigger erratic rhythms, making early detection through monitoring crucial. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T2#GNS212_U4_T2_h1)

question: Why is it smart to adjust alarm limits on a portable monitor for each specific patient?

options.A: The machine will refuse to record data without personalized input
options.B: Standard defaults are illegal to use in modern hospitals
options.C: Customizing limits stops the battery from draining too quickly
options.D: Factory defaults may be unsafe or cause unnecessary alarm fatigue

explanation: Generic settings can either miss a real problem or beep constantly for no reason (alarm fatigue). Tailoring it to the patient keeps everyone sane and safe!

question: Which step of the nursing process involves checking if the patient got better after your advice?

options.A: Planning
options.B: Evaluation
options.C: Diagnosis
options.D: Assessment

explanation: You got it! Evaluation is our final check where we look back at our care plan to see if the patient's condition improved and if our goals were met.

question: What is a major cause of unsafe injection risks in informal healthcare settings?

options.A: Mandatory training for birth attendants
options.B: Too much government checking of pharmacies
options.C: An oversupply of safety boxes
options.D: Not enough clean, single-use equipment available

explanation: When places lack a steady supply of cheap, disposable syringes, dangerous reuse habits can creep in. Community health education helps fix this!

question: A patient with gallbladder trouble feels pain up near their right shoulder blade. What is this called?

options.A: Referred pain
options.B: Phantom pain
options.C: Rebound tenderness
options.D: Somatic pain

explanation: Referred pain happens when internal organs and skin areas share the same spinal cord pathways, tricking the brain into feeling the pain somewhere else.

question: When setting up a ventilator for an adult patient, which measurement is used to calculate the starting tidal volume?

options.A: Actual admission weight
options.B: Height plus blood pressure
options.C: Total body surface area
options.D: Ideal body weight

explanation: Lung size depends on a person's skeletal frame and height, not extra body fat. That's why we use ideal body weight to avoid overinflating their lungs!

question: What is a common ethical worry when patients use modern smart assistive devices?

options.A: Loss of personal privacy through continuous health data collection
options.B: Excessive face-to-face interaction with hospital staff
options.C: Immediate destruction of all electronic health records
options.D: Uncontrolled increases in physical nursing workloads

explanation: Correct! Smart devices often track daily movements and health stats, which raises real questions about keeping patient data private.

question: When we talk about the maternal mortality ratio, what exactly are we measuring?

options.A: Deaths of mothers per 100,000 live births
options.B: Total number of pregnant women in a country
options.C: Number of complicated deliveries per hospital
options.D: Deaths of infants under one year of age

explanation: You've got this! The maternal mortality ratio is simply the number of maternal deaths for every 100,000 live births. It helps us track and improve safety for mothers.

question: How many pairs of spinal nerves are connected to the human spinal cord?

options.A: 31 pairs
options.B: 20 pairs
options.C: 45 pairs
options.D: 12 pairs

question: Which of these is NOT a benefit of knowing research classifications for a nurse?

options.A: Selecting safe treatments backed by strong studies
options.B: Understanding professional nursing journals easily
options.C: Designing simple nursing projects during training
options.D: Diagnosing complex medical conditions independently

question: Which anxiety condition involves sudden, unexpected waves of intense terror and pounding heart palpitations?

options.A: Panic disorder
options.B: Specific phobia
options.C: Generalized anxiety disorder
options.D: Social anxiety disorder

explanation: Spot on! Panic disorder is famous for these sudden, scary attacks out of nowhere, leaving the person worried about when the next one might strike.

question: Which symptom is a major red flag for intrahepatic cholestasis of pregnancy?

options.A: Painful blisters forming exclusively around the mouth
options.B: Rapid darkening of the skin over the entire body
options.C: Severe itching on the palms and soles without an initial rash

question: What is a direct benefit of using research-backed repositioning schedules on the ward?

options.A: An increase in daily patient discharge rates
options.B: A reduction in hospital-acquired pressure ulcers
options.C: Fewer mandatory shifts for junior nurses
options.D: Lower hospital electricity and utility bills

question: How does the cardiovascular center in the medulla help regulate blood pressure?

options.A: By releasing digestive enzymes into the blood
options.B: By producing red blood cells in the bone marrow
options.C: By adjusting heart rate and blood vessel diameter
options.D: By filtering excess water out of the bloodstream

question: Which of these is a common myth about infection control in home settings?

options.A: That handwashing helps reduce bacterial spread

options.C: That the home environment is naturally germ-free
options.D: That used needles require special puncture-proof containers

question: Why is feeling deeply distressed after a disaster considered a normal human reaction?

options.A: Because everyone experiences identical symptoms of grief

options.C: Because the event itself is abnormal and threatening to safety
options.D: Because medical treatment is rarely needed for shock

question: A nurse knows two nurses must verify insulin, but regularly injects it alone during busy shifts to save time. What type of behavior is this?

options.A: Human error
options.B: Reckless behavior
options.C: At-risk behavior
options.D: Systemic malfunction

explanation: Taking shortcuts because it feels faster is an at-risk behavior. It calls for friendly coaching, not panic!

question: What is a major challenge that often stops clients from completing a family planning referral?

options.A: High transportation costs and distance to the receiving facility
options.B: Excessive availability of feedback slips in the primary clinic
options.C: Having too many free contraceptive options available at home
options.D: Too much emotional support provided by community health nurses

explanation: Long distances and transport money wahala are real hurdles that can discourage clients from making the trip to a secondary center.

question: Which underlying societal belief most drives the practice of breast ironing?

options.B: Expecting all young girls to participate in military service
options.C: Blaming female physical development for male sexual misconduct
options.D: Requiring women to alter their bodies for traditional marriage

question: Which antenatal practice helps prevent prolonged labour complications in our communities?

options.A: Identifying high-risk women and planning facility delivery

options.C: Prescribing bed rest for all pregnant women after twenty weeks
options.D: Discouraging any form of physical activity throughout pregnancy

explanation: Excellent! Good antenatal screening lets us spot potential risks early so mothers can plan to deliver safely where expert help is available.

question: Why does dead heart muscle (necrosis) increase the risk of the heart wall tearing open?

options.A: Dead tissue instantly turns into hard bone

options.C: Dead cells make the heart grow too fast
options.D: Blood pressure inside the heart drops to zero

question: Why might crops grown in a specific area lack essential minerals?

options.A: Sunlight destroys minerals inside plants.
options.B: The local water supply is too salty.
options.C: The local soil is missing those trace elements.
options.D: Farmers wash crops with strong chemicals.

explanation: Plants take up nutrients straight from the earth. If the dirt is lacking a specific mineral, the food harvested from it will lack it too!

question: Which nutritional shortage is most commonly linked to tiredness and poor school performance in teenagers?

options.A: Iron deficiency anemia
options.B: Sodium overload
options.C: Excess protein intake
options.D: Vitamin C toxicity

question: Which type of food hazard includes cleaning chemicals and leftover pesticide sprays?

options.A: Physical hazards
options.B: Biological hazards
options.C: Nutritional hazards
options.D: Chemical hazards

question: Which of these is considered a simple, low-tech assistive device?

options.A: A computerized communication board
options.B: A manual reacher
options.C: A motorized wheelchair
options.D: A robotic rehabilitation suit

question: What is the main difference between the two sides of the Loop of Henle?

options.A: The descending limb performs active secretion, while the ascending limb performs filtration.

question: Which pathway carries nerve signals toward the central nervous system?

options.A: Sympathetic division
options.B: Efferent division
options.C: Afferent division
options.D: Autonomic division

question: How should a nurse instruct a patient to use nystatin oral suspension for mouth thrush?

options.A: Swallow the liquid immediately on an empty stomach with a full glass of water
options.B: Swish the liquid thoroughly around the mouth before swallowing it
options.C: Dilute the entire bottle in a glass of cold fruit juice and drink it fast
options.D: Gargle the liquid at the back of the throat and spit it out without swallowing

explanation: Correct! The medication needs time to touch all the infected spots in the mouth before it is swallowed down to coat the throat or gut.

question: What is the main way classic quinoline antimalarial drugs work?

options.A: Binding directly to human liver cell receptors
options.B: Destroying the nervous system of the mosquito vector
options.C: Preventing the detoxification of heme inside the parasite
options.D: Enhancing the production of red blood cells in bone marrow

explanation: Well done! As the parasite digests red blood cells, it releases toxic heme. Quinoline drugs stop the parasite from turning this heme into safe crystals, effectively poisoning it.

question: What is the single biggest risk factor for developing osteoarthritis?

options.A: Regular aerobic exercise
options.B: High dietary sugar
options.C: Advanced age
options.D: Cold weather climates

explanation: That is correct! As we grow older, our joints experience years of natural use, making age the number one risk factor for joint wear and tear.

question: What is the primary focus of Psychological First Aid (PFA) delivered by nurses after a disaster?

options.A: Offering practical support, comfort, and addressing basic needs
options.B: Prescribing strong antipsychotic medications to all adult survivors
options.C: Conducting deep psychoanalysis and forced trauma debriefing
options.D: Diagnosing long-term clinical depression within the first hour

explanation: PFA is about being a comforting human presence, helping survivors feel safe and meeting their immediate needs without pushing them to talk about trauma.

question: If Florence Nightingale could whisper advice to you on the ward today, what would she say is the true focus of nursing?

options.A: Diagnosing rare tropical medical diseases
options.B: Manipulating the patient's environment to promote healing
options.C: Performing major surgical procedures
options.D: Administering complex intravenous medications

explanation: You got it! Nightingale was all about fresh air, clean water, and bright light. She believed in setting up the environment so the patient's body could heal itself.

question: How do open, uncovered infectious waste bins help spread diseases in the community?

options.A: By attracting disease-carrying vectors like insects and rodents
options.B: By causing airborne chemical burns among nearby residents
options.C: By lowering the ambient temperature to preserve bacteria
options.D: By releasing toxic radiation into the local water supply

explanation: Flies, rats, and mosquitoes love exposed waste. They feed on it and then carry those dangerous germs straight into our living areas!

question: What usually stops teenagers from visiting clinics for reproductive health issues?

options.A: Mandatory free distribution of supplies in schools
options.B: A complete absence of hospitals in urban centers
options.C: Fear of being judged and a lack of privacy from staff
options.D: Strict laws requiring adolescent doctors for teenage patients

explanation: Teens often avoid seeking help because they are scared healthcare workers will gossip, judge them, or break their trust. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T8#GNS216_U1_T8_h7)

question: When an artificial intelligence alert pops up on a patient monitor, what should the nurse do?

options.A: Discharge the patient immediately based on the computer screen
options.B: Ignore the patient completely because the computer is always right
options.C: Turn off all hospital monitors so they stop making noise
options.D: Evaluate the alert and use clinical judgment to decide the next step

explanation: Technology is a support tool, and nurses must always apply their own professional assessment before taking action. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T1#GNS113_U3_T1_h6)

question: What normal change in stool appearance should you explain to a patient after a barium enema?

options.A: Bright neon green liquid
options.B: Chalky white or pale gray color
options.C: Bright red blood streaks in every stool
options.D: Dark black and sticky consistency

explanation: As the body passes out the leftover barium contrast, the stool naturally turns a pale, chalky shade for a couple of days. It is completely normal!

question: Why do many patients hide their use of traditional home remedies from doctors and nurses?

options.A: Herbal remedies leave no physical trace in the body
options.B: Fear of being scolded or dismissed by healthcare providers
options.C: They believe nurses already monitor everything they ingest
options.D: Because hospital rules forbid talking about home treatments

explanation: Exactly. Patients often stay quiet because they worry healthcare workers will judge or mock their cultural healing practices.

question: A hospital safety committee has limited funds and must fix hazards. Which risk should they tackle first?

options.A: A frequent risk that can cause permanent patient disability
options.B: A rare risk that causes a minor inconvenience to visitors
options.C: A paperwork delay that does not affect direct patient care
options.D: A one-time complaint about the taste of the drinking water

explanation: Risks with high frequency and severe consequences demand immediate action to prevent serious patient harm. [learn more](GST319_U4_T6#GST319_U4_T6_h3)

question: Why is 'closed-loop communication' so important during a chaotic resuscitation?

options.A: It prevents the doctor from having to touch the patient
options.B: It confirms that instructions given by the team leader are clearly heard and executed
options.C: It ensures that family members outside the room stay quiet
options.D: It reduces the need for documentation after the code is over

explanation: Brilliant! Repeating instructions back (like 'Giving 1mg epinephrine now') stops dangerous mistakes when things get loud and fast.

question: Why is self-care considered a professional duty for nurses working in disaster zones?

options.A: It guarantees a higher salary during emergency deployments
options.B: It ensures the nurse remains healthy enough to provide safe patient care
options.C: It allows the nurse to avoid interacting with difficult patients
options.D: It proves to the hospital management that the nurse is working hard

explanation: A nurse who is completely burned out and emotionally depleted cannot effectively care for vulnerable patients. [learn more](GNS315_U5_T6#GNS315_U5_T6_h8)

question: Which of the following is NOT a necessary step when receiving new stock on the ward?

options.A: Verifying that the expiration dates on the products are acceptable
options.B: Checking the physical items against the quantities on the delivery note
options.C: Hiding the delivery notes so other staff members cannot read them
options.D: Inspecting the packaging for any signs of damage or leakage

explanation: Delivery notes are official records that should be kept accessible for audits, not hidden away. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T14#GNS122_U3_T14_h6)

question: A woman at home experiences heavy vaginal bleeding shortly after delivering the placenta. What should the nurse do FIRST?

options.A: Send a family member to buy oral iron supplements from a local shop
options.B: Wait for thirty minutes to see if the bleeding stops on its own
options.C: Perform immediate uterine massage and administer oxytocin
options.D: Document the estimated blood loss in the register

explanation: Uterine massage and uterotonic drugs stimulate contractions to clamp down open blood vessels and stop the bleeding immediately. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T15#GNS324_U3_T15_h4)

question: Why is the skin considered a window into a patient's general health status?

options.A: It is the only body organ that nurses can touch easily
options.B: The skin produces all the hormones needed to run the body
options.C: Skin cells grow faster than any other cells in the body
options.D: Changes in skin color and texture often reflect internal organ problems

explanation: Systemic illnesses frequently show visible signs on the skin, such as jaundice for liver issues or pallor for anemia. [learn more](GNS211_U2_T5#GNS211_U2_T5_h8)

question: You walk into a patient's room and see a big loop of chest tube tubing resting on the floor. What should you do first?

options.C: Adjust the tubing so it coils loosely on the bed and drains freely without kinks
options.D: Disconnect the tubing joints to empty the pooled fluid onto the floor

question: When helping a stroke patient with left-sided weakness put on a button-down shirt, which arm goes in first?

options.C: The right arm

question: What does a flashing red light or a chirping sound on an AED usually mean?

options.A: The AED battery is fully charged and ready for an emergency.
