question: Which communication technique helps encourage a patient to open up about their feelings?

options.A: Offering false reassurance
options.B: Changing the conversation topic
options.C: Giving immediate advice
options.D: Asking open-ended questions

explanation: Open-ended questions (like 'How have you been sleeping lately?') invite patients to share their story freely instead of just nodding with a simple yes or no.

question: Why are psychiatric nurses often the first to spot early signs of relapse in parole patients?

options.A: They spend all their time reviewing legal documents in offices.
options.B: They have close, regular contact through home visits and clinic checks.
options.C: They hold the sole legal power to revoke parole on their own.
options.D: They are the only healthcare workers trained in mental health.

explanation: Exactly! Because nurses build close bonds and check in regularly, they are usually the first to notice subtle shifts in a patient's behavior.

question: Which component must be identical in both generic and brand name drugs?

options.A: The retail price in the pharmacy
options.B: The proprietary marketing title
options.C: The active pharmaceutical ingredient
options.D: The inactive coloring dyes

explanation: Regulatory bodies ensure that whether you buy the expensive brand name or the affordable generic, the active healing ingredient inside is 100% the same.

question: Why do cooks love adding waterleaf to traditional Nigerian soups and stews?

options.A: It turns the broth into a solid gel when allowed to cool down
options.B: It serves as a strong preservative to keep soups from spoiling quickly
options.C: It acts as a natural thickening agent while adding moisture and vitamins
options.D: It completely replaces the need for adding palm oil to the pot

explanation: Spot on! Waterleaf breaks down nicely during cooking to give soups a rich texture while boosting the vitamin content.

question: Why is the infant mortality rate considered a sensitive indicator of a community's general health status?

options.A: It shows the exact number of elderly people suffering from chronic heart conditions
options.B: It measures the total financial wealth of households in the region
options.C: It reflects the quality of maternal and child health services and living conditions
options.D: It is the easiest statistic for local government officials to calculate manually

explanation: Infant survival depends heavily on clean water, nutrition, and good healthcare, making it a reliable mirror of overall community well-being. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T4#GNS124_U3_T4_h3)

question: What type of measurement expresses a part as a fraction of the whole, often as a percentage?

options.A: Rate
options.B: Proportion
options.C: Ratio
options.D: Incidence

explanation: That's correct! A proportion takes a subgroup and compares it directly to the total population. You're doing great with these public health terms!

question: What happens to complement protein levels (such as C3 and C4) in the blood during active serum sickness?

options.A: They decrease
options.B: They disappear entirely
options.C: They remain completely normal
options.D: They increase

explanation: Think of complement proteins as fuel used up in a fire; because the immune reaction is working overtime, these levels drop in the blood.

question: A hospital needs a powerful system to manage records for thousands of patients at the same time. Which type of computer is best suited for this?

options.A: A single pocket calculator
options.B: A simple analog wave measuring tool
options.C: A large central system like a mainframe
options.D: A basic desktop microcomputer with no network

explanation: You got it! Mainframes are the heavy lifters of the hospital world, built to handle massive networks and data for entire institutions all at once.

question: Why are healthcare workers sometimes at higher risk for developing substance use issues?

options.A: They are completely exempt from the legal penalties of drug abuse
options.B: They experience heavy job stress and have easy access to medications
options.C: They receive special training on how to safely consume illegal substances
options.D: They possess a genetic immunity that makes them careless with drugs

explanation: The intense stress of clinical life combined with being around drugs all day creates a tough environment. Looking out for our mental health as nurses is so important!

question: What is the recommended chest compression rate per minute for an adult in cardiac arrest?

options.A: 140 to 160 compressions per minute
options.B: 100 to 120 compressions per minute
options.C: 60 to 80 compressions per minute
options.D: 40 to 60 compressions per minute

explanation: A rate of 100 to 120 per minute mimics a normal working heart rate to push blood forward effectively. [learn more](GNS315_U4_T4#GNS315_U4_T4_h2)

question: How does immunotherapy work differently from standard chemotherapy?

options.A: It completely replaces the need for any diagnostic imaging procedures.
options.B: It only acts on the outer layer of the skin and never reaches the lungs.
options.C: It freezes the tumor tissue by lowering the core body temperature.
options.D: It empowers the body's own immune defenses to target and destroy cancer cells.

explanation: Exactly right! Instead of just attacking cells directly like chemo, immunotherapy helps your own white blood cells recognize and fight off the cancer.

question: Which of the following is an effective strategy for reducing household expenditure on proteins without sacrificing nutrition?

options.A: Buying imported specialty protein powders instead of whole foods
options.B: Purchasing single-serving pre-packaged meals from restaurants
options.C: Removing all forms of protein entirely from the family diet
options.D: Replacing expensive meat cuts with plant-based options like beans and lentils

explanation: Plant proteins offer high nutritional value at a fraction of the cost of red meat or poultry. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T015#GNS227_U4_T015_h3)

question: What is the main focus of modern recovery-oriented psychiatric nursing?

options.A: Confining patients indefinitely in secure institutional facilities
options.B: Helping individuals live meaningful lives despite mental health challenges
options.C: Relying exclusively on physical restraints during behavioral crises
options.D: Ignoring social factors in favor of strict medication compliance

explanation: Today's psychiatric nursing is all about recovery. We empower patients to chase their personal goals, live independently, and find real wellness.

question: A ward nurse carefully checks expiry dates and avoids opening extra sterile packs during a procedure. What is the nurse showing?

options.A: Risk pooling
options.B: Equity
options.C: Efficiency
options.D: Vertical integration

explanation: Spot on! Preventing waste in the ward is a practical way nurses practice efficiency every single day.

question: What is the main goal of Behavioural Change Communication (BCC) in public health?

options.A: To diagnose complex chronic medical conditions
options.B: To guide people toward positive health practices
options.C: To distribute free prescription medications
options.D: To enforce strict health laws in rural areas

explanation: Spot on! BCC is all about using engaging conversations and communication to help people and communities build and keep healthy lifestyle habits.

question: Who takes the lead in providing support at Tier 2 of the MHPSS pyramid?

options.A: Neurosurgeons and clinical pharmacologists
options.B: Community members, family networks, and local leaders
options.C: Only certified trauma therapists
options.D: International psychiatric researchers

explanation: You got it! Tier 2 relies heavily on everyday people—family, friends, and community leaders—helping each other cope through social connection.

question: Which of these habits helps keep oral syringes clean and free of germs?

options.A: Rinsing the dirty syringe in a shared sink basin
options.B: Storing open syringes in a warm pocket all day
options.C: Avoiding touching the syringe tip to any surface
options.D: Touching the tip directly to the patient's tongue

explanation: Keep that tip sterile! Touching it to counters or fingers can introduce unwanted bacteria right back into the medicine bottle.

question: What is the primary aim of culturally sensitive nutrition counseling in nursing?

options.A: Forcing patients to abandon their cultural heritage completely
options.B: Convincing doctors to change hospital meal timetables
options.C: Replacing all local dishes with imported western food items
options.D: Finding acceptable local food substitutes that maintain good nutrition

explanation: We don't need to fight a patient's culture! Instead, we work with what they have, suggesting safe, affordable local foods that provide the exact same nutrients.

question: What is an asymptomatic carrier?

options.A: A host who harbors an infectious agent without showing illness but can still spread it
options.B: A patient who has completely recovered and has lifelong immunity to a virus
options.C: An environmental surface that holds bacteria without allowing them to multiply
options.D: An animal that serves as the final dead-end host for a dangerous parasite

explanation: An asymptomatic carrier feels totally fine and shows no signs of sickness, but they are secretly carrying and spreading the germ to others.

question: A patient keeps returning to the clinic with waterborne infections due to poor living conditions. What do these conditions represent?

options.A: Social determinants of health
options.B: An acute pharmaceutical side effect
options.C: A failure of individual personal hygiene
options.D: A rare genetic immune system disorder

explanation: Living conditions like clean water access are environmental and social factors that directly dictate health status. [learn more](GST321_U6_T3#GST321_U6_T3_h5)

question: What does the term 'adverse selection' mean in community health insurance?

options.A: Doctors refuse to treat patients with insurance cards
options.B: Hospitals run out of essential drugs during emergencies
options.C: Only sick people join while healthy people stay out
options.D: The government cancels the health scheme suddenly

explanation: Adverse selection is a tricky challenge. When mostly sick people join and healthy people skip it, the insurance pool runs out of money because payouts are way higher than collected funds.

question: If a ward suddenly sees many more surgical site infections because of a poorly sterilized batch of tools, what kind of variation is this?

options.A: Special cause variation
options.B: Common cause variation
options.C: Standard baseline variation
options.D: Theoretical variation

explanation: This is a special cause variation because it is an unexpected, unusual event caused by a specific problem that needs fixing right away.

question: Why are hospital utility bills counted as 'indirect costs'?

options.A: They are shared across the facility and cannot be tied to one patient
options.B: They are paid directly by the nursing department
options.C: They only apply to private hospital rooms
options.D: They change every single day based on the weather

explanation: Things like electricity and water keep the whole hospital running for everyone, so you can't assign them to just one single patient's bill.

question: If you notice that a broken borehole is causing waterborne illnesses, what role are you mainly playing?

options.A: Hospital administrator
options.B: Surgical assistant
options.C: Needs assessor
options.D: Pharmacist

explanation: Spot on! Spotting a health issue and tracing it back to environmental problems is what a needs assessment is all about.

question: What does the 'mode' tell us about a set of data?

options.A: The exact middle point of sorted values
options.B: The value that occurs most frequently
options.C: The average of all recorded numbers
options.D: The distance between extremes

explanation: Think of the mode as the most popular or frequently repeated number in your dataset. Easy peasy!

question: Why is getting the right specimen so important for prescribing antibiotics?

options.A: It allows doctors to prescribe targeted therapy rather than guessing
options.B: It prevents nurses from needing to wear sterile gloves
options.C: It ensures the patient receives the strongest drug available immediately
options.D: It lowers the financial cost of hospital room maintenance

explanation: When we know the exact bug, the doctor can give the right drug instead of just guessing. That stops antibiotic resistance and helps the patient heal faster!

question: Which of these is NOT a common challenge when different health sectors try to work together?

options.A: Weak communication and rules
options.B: Differing goals and priorities
options.C: Cultural mistrust between public and private workers
options.D: Universal agreement on profit margins

explanation: Sectors almost never agree easily on profit margins! Public and non-profit groups focus on health equity, while for-profit groups focus on returns.

question: A rural clinic sees a sudden cluster of Hepatitis C cases all linked to the same treatment room. What does this point to?

options.A: A natural seasonal variation in viral mutations
options.B: A community outbreak driven by unsafe clinical practices
options.C: An airborne respiratory infection spreading through the ward
options.D: A foodborne intoxication from contaminated local water

explanation: When multiple blood-borne infections pop up tied to one facility, it usually points to a breakdown in basic infection control and sterilization. Excellent clinical deduction!

question: What does the term "not-invented-here syndrome" mean in a hospital setting?

options.A: Staff reject a new practice simply because they did not come up with it themselves
options.B: Nurses refuse to care for patients admitted from another hospital
options.C: Management bans any new clinical guidelines written by outside experts
options.D: The hospital refuses to buy medical equipment made in foreign countries

explanation: Have you ever seen people reject a good idea just because it wasn't their own? That's 'not-invented-here syndrome'—a common human habit we learn to overcome!

question: What is the best way for a nurse to find out if a patient is trying a risky diet?

options.A: Scolding the patient immediately for reading health advice online
options.B: Asking open-ended questions about how the patient manages their weight
options.C: Threatening to report the use of herbal supplements to the hospital board
options.D: Refusing to provide medical care until the patient stops buying vitamins

explanation: Patients won't open up if you judge them. Friendly, open-ended questions make them feel safe to tell the truth. You're going to be a great nurse!

question: How do electronic records make a nurse's daily work easier compared to old paper charts?

options.A: By shortening the required length of a hospital stay for surgery
options.B: By eliminating the need to ever measure patient vital signs
options.C: By reducing medication errors caused by poor handwriting
options.D: By removing all documentation duties from the nursing staff

explanation: Great job! We've all struggled to read messy handwriting. Digital records clear that up so nobody gives the wrong drug by mistake.

question: Which of the following is NOT a helpful way to encourage eating in a frail older adult?

options.A: Forcing the patient to finish large meals within a strict time limit
options.B: Ensuring dentures are clean and placed in the mouth before mealtime
options.C: Creating a quiet, pleasant environment free from clinical distractions
options.D: Offering frequent small meals and nutrient-dense snacks throughout the day

explanation: You got it! Forcing big meals on someone with a poor appetite can be overwhelming. Smaller, frequent plates and a calm atmosphere work wonders instead!

question: Why do dialogue groups involving village elders and men help improve women's health access?

options.A: They address cultural norms that restrict women from seeking care
options.B: They replace the professional nursing staff in maternal wards
options.C: They prevent women from leaving their homes for any reason
options.D: They give men exclusive control over clinic budgets and supplies

explanation: You got it! Since elders and men often hold decision-making power in the home, getting them on board helps remove cultural blocks that stop women from getting timely care.

question: What is the main job of satellite cells in our skeletal muscles?

options.A: To repair and regenerate damaged muscle fibers
options.B: To remove lactic acid buildup after heavy exercise
options.C: To store calcium ions needed for sliding filaments
options.D: To produce the nerve signals that trigger contraction

explanation: Satellite cells are like little standby repair crew members. When muscle gets injured, they jump in to help fix and rebuild it!

question: Why do human-made disasters often catch us off guard and create complex challenges?

options.A: They only affect critical infrastructure and leave human populations unharmed
options.B: They strike suddenly without warning and leave behind persistent secondary dangers
options.C: They are easily contained and never require outside medical assistance
options.D: They completely eliminate the risk of subsequent environmental contamination

explanation: Great thinking! Because these events happen without warning and leave behind things like toxic smoke or weak buildings, they keep emergency responders on high alert.

question: Why is integrating basic mental health services into primary healthcare clinics an effective strategy?

options.A: It stops patients from ever needing medication in the future
options.B: It guarantees that patients will never experience stress again
options.C: It makes mental health care more accessible and reduces social stigma
options.D: It eliminates the need for any nurses or doctors to be present

explanation: When mental health care is offered right inside regular primary clinics, patients can seek help easily without the shame of visiting a specialized psychiatric hospital. [learn more](GNS314_U1_T7#GNS314_U1_T7_h8)

question: What does a growing GDP fail to guarantee regarding a national health system?

options.A: That nurses will receive higher salaries
options.B: That the country will stop importing medications
options.C: That the wealth will automatically translate into better healthcare access
options.D: That hospitals will have electricity every day

explanation: Economic growth provides potential revenue, but political will and budget priorities dictate whether that money actually reaches clinics and patients.

question: What is the core question asked during a Root Cause Analysis (RCA) investigation?

options.A: Which specific staff member is guilty of negligence?
options.B: Why did the system allow this event to happen?
options.C: How much financial loss did the hospital suffer?
options.D: Who should be fired immediately for this failure?

explanation: RCA is like detective work for processes—we look for broken systems, not bad people.

question: What is the main difference between bacterial and viral STIs in the body?

options.A: Bacterial infections cause permanent cellular mutations, while viral infections do not
options.B: Viral infections remain in the body long-term, while bacterial infections are usually cured
options.C: Viral infections never respond to any form of pharmaceutical treatment
options.D: Bacterial infections require lifelong maintenance therapy instead of short courses

explanation: Spot on! Bacteria can usually be kicked out with medications, but viruses like HIV or herpes stay in the body for life and need long-term management.

question: How can a learning disability affect other children in the family?

options.A: Siblings may experience feelings of neglect or added stress
options.B: Siblings automatically develop the exact same learning disability
options.C: Siblings lose all of their academic abilities
options.D: Siblings are completely unaffected by the situation

explanation: Family dynamics shift when one child requires extensive attention and advocacy, which can impact brothers and sisters emotionally. [learn more](GNS324_U4_T6#GNS324_U4_T6_h7)
